the minimal sequence of pI required for membrane insertion is a 20-resided hydrophobic stretch, but that the minimal sequence for growth inhibition is the same as that for membrane insertion.

the 55-residues of the pI protein contain a 20-residues hydrophobic sequence which is sufficient to translocate a protein across the inner membrane and that the same 20-residures sequence is sufficient to inhibit growth of cells provided it contains domains exposed on both the cytoplamic and periplasmic faces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the minimal membrane insertion domain for the pI protein of bacteriophage f1 is a single hydrophobic stretch of 20 residues.
the membrane translocating sequence of the pI protein consists of 21 residues, the first 10 being positively charged and the last 11 hydrophobic.
the membrane insertion of pI is a relatively simple process requiring the presence of only the 20-residues hydrophobic stretch.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a short, 20-residue, hydrophobic sequence can be sufficient for membrane insertion.
a 21-amino-acid hydrophobic stretch is sufficient for membrane insertion and growth inhibition of a protein.
a single membrane-spanning domain of the phage protein pI can be sufficient to cause growth inhibition.
